items.claim: A node(id:) or nodes(ids:) field on the root Query type exposes a standard mechanism for asking for an object by its global ID, so the object is reachable by ID rather than only through its parent field.

sources.quote: For this to work, a client will need to query via a standard mechanism to request an object by ID.
In the query, the schema should provide a standard mechanism for asking for an object by ID.

items.claim: A resource-exhaustion finding in GraphQL needs evidence of backend cost; depth limiting is not the only control, because a shallow operation with many aliases can amplify load in a single HTTP request.

sources.quote: Query cost analysis involves assigning costs to the resolution of fields or types in incoming queries so that the server can reject queries that cost too much to run or will consume too many resources.
Because aliases effectively enable you to send multiple queries in a single HTTP message, they can bypass this restriction.

This signature prevents attackers, such as a malicious client or user, from forging a token or modifying the claims in an existing token, for example changing the user role from a simple user to an admin or altering the client's login.

It does not only protect against authorization code injection attacks but also protects authorization codes created for public clients as PKCE ensures that the attacker cannot redeem a stolen authorization code at the token endpoint of the authorization server without knowledge of the code_verifier.
If a Client sends a valid PKCE "code_challenge" parameter in the authorization request, the authorization server enforces the correct usage of "code_verifier" at the token endpoint.

Prototype pollution vulnerabilities typically arise when a JavaScript function recursively merges an object containing user-controllable properties into an existing object, without first sanitizing the keys.
These codes can be used to add "isAdmin: true" to the object prototype.

The Microsoft Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) provides remote display and input capabilities over network connections for Windows-based applications running on a server. RDP is designed to support different types of network topologies and multiple LAN protocols.

items.claim: A dangling record that enables takeover can be a CNAME or an A record pointing at a released IP address, so DNS enumeration has to inspect both record types instead of CNAMEs alone.
items.body:
A dangling record that enables takeover can be a CNAME or an A record pointing at a released IP address, so DNS enumeration has to inspect both record types instead of CNAMEs alone.

OWASP notes that A records pointing to released IP addresses can be vulnerable if the IP is reassigned and the attacker obtains it; Microsoft describes the CNAME case where a DNS record points to a deprovisioned Azure resource.

sources.quote: A records pointing to released IP addresses can be vulnerable if the IP is reassigned and the attacker obtains it.
A subdomain takeover can occur when you have a DNS record that points to a deprovisioned Azure resource.
